title: A Friend of Mine, My Own and Being Alone
summary: Describe one member of a group with a friend of mine or a colleague of hers, use my own and similar forms for things not shared or borrowed, and say that someone acts or lives alone with on their own or by themselves.
learningObjectives: Replace one of my/your/her friends with a friend of mine/yours/hers and use other possessive-pronoun forms accurately.
Use a friend of someone's with names and identify how it differs from an ordinary of-phrase.
Choose the correct possessive determiner before own and use own with an understood noun.
Describe doing something without company or assistance using on my own or by myself and matching person/number.

explanation.heading: A friend of mine: one person from a group
explanation.body: To identify one person or thing from a group associated with someone, English often uses a + noun + of + possessive pronoun: a friend of mine, an uncle of hers, a neighbour of ours. The pronoun must be mine, yours, his, hers, ours or theirs, not me, you, him, her, us or them. The pattern can also be plural: some colleagues of theirs. It does not mean that the speaker owns the person.
explanation.example: A neighbour of ours offered to water the plants while we were away.

explanation.heading: A friend of someone's: names and possessives
explanation.body: The same pattern works with names and family expressions: a customer of Lina's, a teammate of my brother's. The possessive ending belongs to the person or people identified after of. It usually indicates one among several people or things related to that person. Keep the article or another appropriate determiner before the first noun; a colleague of Eva's is a complete phrase.
explanation.example: One of the speakers was a former student of Dr Chen's.

explanation.heading: My own: something separate or belonging to me
explanation.body: Use a possessive determiner followed by own: my own, your own, his own, her own, its own, our own or their own. The combination often stresses that something is not shared, provided by someone else or borrowed. Use my own desk rather than an own desk. If the noun is already known, it can be omitted: She uses her own [computer]. You can also say a desk of my own.
explanation.example: The new employee has her own locker instead of sharing one.

explanation.heading: Own for things people create or choose
explanation.body: Own can emphasise personal responsibility, authorship or choice: make your own lunch, grow our own herbs, form their own opinions. In these uses, it is not only a legal claim of possession. Distinguish writing your own report (the report is yours, not someone else's) from writing the report yourself (you did the work personally). Both may be true, but they focus on different ideas.
explanation.example: The workshop participants designed their own posters rather than copying templates.

explanation.heading: On my own and by myself: alone or independently
explanation.body: On my own and by myself normally both mean alone, without company or help. Match the form to the subject: on her own/by herself; on our own/by ourselves; on their own/by themselves. They can describe living alone, travelling without companions or completing a task without assistance. Unlike the emphatic I did it myself, these phrases explicitly suggest that nobody helped or accompanied the person in the relevant situation.
explanation.example: Marta assembled the shelf on her own, without asking anyone for help.

comparisons.title: One among my friends: two natural forms

left.label: Possessive determiner
left.example: One of my friends works at the museum.
left.note: One of my friends selects a person from the group of my friends.

right.label: Double possessive
right.example: A friend of mine works at the museum.
right.note: Of mine expresses the same group relationship after a noun.

left.label: Exclusive personal space
left.note: Own shows she does not have to share the studio.

right.label: Shared space
right.example: Dara shares a studio with two artists.
right.note: No own is used because the studio is shared.

left.label: A personally associated result
left.note: Own identifies whose presentation it is.

right.label: Independent work
right.example: I prepared the presentation on my own.
right.note: On my own says I prepared it without help.

examples.sentence: An old classmate of hers recommended the course.
examples.note: Of hers identifies one person from the group of her classmates.

examples.sentence: That suggestion was an idea of Daniel's.
examples.note: The possessive ending is attached to Daniel after of.

examples.sentence: The cyclists brought their own water bottles.
examples.note: Their own highlights that the bottles were personally supplied, not shared.

examples.sentence: My phone is charging, so you can use your own.
examples.note: Own stands for your own phone because phone is already understood.

examples.sentence: Rosa went to the exhibition by herself because her friends were busy.
examples.note: By herself explains that Rosa had no companion on the visit.

commonMistakes.incorrect: A colleague of me sent the invitation.
commonMistakes.correct: A colleague of mine sent the invitation.
commonMistakes.why: After of in this double-possessive pattern, use mine, not the object pronoun me.

commonMistakes.incorrect: He is a friend of Nadia.
commonMistakes.correct: He is a friend of Nadia's.
commonMistakes.why: To mean one of Nadia's friends, the standard double-possessive pattern uses Nadia's.

commonMistakes.correct: The guests brought their own food.
commonMistakes.why: Own needs a possessive determiner such as their.
A plural subject needs the plural reflexive form themselves after by.

studyTips: Transform pairs in writing: one of our neighbours → a neighbour of ours; one of her cousins → a cousin of hers.
When you see own, check for the possessive determiner immediately before it and decide whether the noun can be omitted.
Practise pairs aloud: He owns the equipment; he has his own equipment; he installed it on his own. Notice the different meanings.

exercises.prompt: Kai lives next door to us. He is a neighbour ___.
exercises.feedback: A neighbour of ours means one of our neighbours; ours is a possessive pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Nadia no longer wants to share a laptop. She needs ___.
exercises.feedback: Own follows the possessive determiner her; it emphasises a laptop she does not share.

exercises.prompt: The suggestion came from Marco, not me. It was an idea ___.
exercises.feedback: An idea of Marco's identifies one of Marco's ideas using the name in possessive form.

exercises.prompt: No guide or friend joined Leila on the hike. She completed it ___.
exercises.feedback: On her own means without help or company; by herself would also be natural.

exercises.prompt: This is one of my cousins. He is a cousin of ___ . (one word: possessive pronoun)
exercises.feedback: Use the possessive pronoun mine after of, not the object pronoun me.

exercises.prompt: Sofia knows Priya through work. Sofia is a colleague of ___ . (write Priya in its possessive form)
exercises.feedback: A colleague of Priya's means one of Priya's colleagues.

exercises.prompt: We do not borrow equipment from the other team. We use ___ equipment. (two words: possessive determiner + own)
exercises.feedback: Our own marks equipment belonging to or reserved for our team.

exercises.prompt: I had no help with the translation. I finished it ___ . (three words; begin with on)
exercises.feedback: On my own expresses completing the task independently.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: A teammate of me checked the schedule.
acceptedAnswers: A teammate of mine checked the schedule.
exercises.feedback: After of, a person associated with the speaker is described using mine.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence by changing only the incorrect article: She doesn't have an own office yet.
acceptedAnswers: She doesn't have her own office yet.
exercises.feedback: Use the possessive determiner her before own; an own is not a valid noun phrase here.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: That is a suggestion of their's.
acceptedAnswers: That is a suggestion of theirs.
exercises.feedback: The possessive pronoun theirs has no apostrophe.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The children finished the puzzle by theirselves.
acceptedAnswers: The children finished the puzzle by themselves.
exercises.feedback: Use the plural reflexive themselves after by with the children.

speakingExercises.prompt: Rephrase the supplied sentence, starting with A friend of mine and ending with yesterday: One of my friends called yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: A friend of mine called yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: A friend of mine is equivalent to one of my friends.

speakingExercises.prompt: Rephrase in the active voice. Begin with A colleague of Aisha's and end with arranged the meeting: One of Aisha's colleagues arranged the meeting.
acceptedAnswers: A colleague of Aisha's arranged the meeting.
speakingExercises.feedback: The double possessive keeps Aisha's after of.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one sentence using these facts: Maya / have / her own office / now. Start with Maya and end with now. Use the present simple.
acceptedAnswers: Maya has her own office now.
speakingExercises.feedback: The singular subject Maya takes has; her own office means an office not shared.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend offers to lend you a charger, but you already have one. Reply with one sentence beginning I have and ending my own charger. Do not add got.
speakingExercises.feedback: My own charger explains that a borrowed one is unnecessary.

speakingExercises.prompt: Keep the preposition on, correct the expression that follows it, and say the complete sentence: Leo travelled on himself.
speakingExercises.feedback: On his own is the natural phrase for travelling alone.

speakingExercises.prompt: Two designers completed the prototype without assistance. State this in one sentence beginning with The designers and ending with by themselves. Use finished the prototype.
acceptedAnswers: The designers finished the prototype by themselves.
speakingExercises.feedback: By themselves means the two designers finished without outside help.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say exactly two sentences from these facts. First: I / make / my own lunch / every day (present simple). Second: I / usually eat / on my own. Use no contractions.
acceptedAnswers: I make my own lunch every day. I usually eat on my own.
speakingExercises.feedback: My own describes the lunch I make; on my own describes eating alone.

speakingExercises.prompt: Your group has a shared office, but Tara has a room only for herself. State one sentence beginning Tara and ending at work. Use have in the present simple and the phrase her own room.
acceptedAnswers: Tara has her own room at work.
speakingExercises.feedback: Her own identifies a room reserved for Tara rather than shared with the group.

listeningExercises.prompt: How does the speaker know the teacher?
choices: The teacher previously taught the speaker’s brother.
The teacher works with the speaker now.
listeningExercises.feedback: A former teacher of my brother's identifies a teaching connection with the brother.
listeningExercises.audioText: The speaker at tomorrow's event is a former teacher of my brother's, not one of my teachers.

listeningExercises.prompt: What has changed for the students?
choices: Each student now has a separate camera.
listeningExercises.feedback: Their own camera contrasts individually available equipment with borrowed college cameras.
listeningExercises.audioText: We used to borrow cameras from the college, but this year each student has their own camera.

listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression immediately after An old.
listeningExercises.feedback: Friend of mine uses a possessive pronoun after of.
listeningExercises.audioText: An old friend of mine works in the theatre's ticket office.

choices: A mechanic hired by the speaker.
The person who made the tutorial.
listeningExercises.feedback: On my own shows the speaker completed the repair without a mechanic.
listeningExercises.audioText: I didn't ask a mechanic to fix the bicycle. I repaired it on my own after watching a tutorial.

choices: Her colleagues wrote the speech for her.
Olivia wrote the speech and later received feedback.
Nobody else read the speech before the event.
listeningExercises.feedback: Her own speech identifies Olivia as the writer, while colleagues checked it later.
listeningExercises.audioText: Olivia wrote her own speech, but she asked her colleagues to check the spelling before the event.

listeningExercises.prompt: What was different during the summer?
choices: Tom moved into a larger flat.
Tom lived without his usual flatmates.
listeningExercises.feedback: By himself means Tom lived alone while his flatmates were away.
listeningExercises.audioText: Tom usually shares a flat with two friends. During the summer, both friends travelled abroad, so he lived by himself.

listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word expression immediately before supplies.
listeningExercises.feedback: Their own stresses supplies bought for the artists rather than shared equipment.
listeningExercises.audioText: After years of sharing equipment, the artists finally bought their own supplies.

listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word expression immediately after route.
listeningExercises.feedback: By herself indicates completing the route alone.
listeningExercises.audioText: The youngest participant finished the route by herself, without a guide.
